summary.text:
Wrong entity for our platform. This is the treasury management strategy of the Isle of Wight Pension Fund, not the council — a distinct legal balance sheet ring-fenced from the council per paragraph 16 of the covering report. The paper deals with the fund's internally-managed operating cash: £10.0m at 31 March 2026 across a Lloyds high-interest account (£6.5m at 3.51%) and two Money Market Funds (Aberdeen £1.5m and Aviva £2.0m, both at 3.81%), plus £0.591m in the Lloyds pension fund current account, all managed by the council's treasury team with Arlingclose advising and an A- credit floor.

There is no CFR, no PWLB borrowing, no prudential indicator table and no MRP policy — a pension fund has none of those. Paragraph 11 of the appendix confirms the fund is not borrowing. The only forward change is a governance one: 'Fit for the Future' will migrate investment cash to the asset pool company, leaving operational cash with the administering authority but subject to reporting.

Nothing on this paper reconciles to the council's own PWLB book. Our file separately shows the council (borrower name 'ISLE OF WIGHT COUNCIL') holds 26 PWLB loans totalling £135.19m at a weighted 3.11% at 31 March 2026 — that is context, not a check against this paper. No email drafted: a PWLB-borrowing pitch off a pension-fund cash paper would come out of nothing, and the paper simply does not put a council-treasury signal in front of us.
